messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency > 5s for dedicated pool d-nj-2 (model: redwood/open-13b). Streaming stalls observed; tail latency spike around 16:46 UTC. Auto-escalation to #incidents triggered :rotating_light:
Irina (oncall): acked. i'm on it, pulling traces and pool metrics. any customers impacted yet?
Tom: looking at autoscaler logs now. seeing repeated warmup handshake timeouts between orchestrator <-> worker: `handshake_timeout=120s` spikes at 16:44. queue depth for d-nj-2 jumped from 12->420 in ~2m.
Juan: confirmed. warmup throttle backed up; workers in that pool failed to register due to attachment errors to nfs mount. errors: `mount timeout` and `failed to fetch init weights` in logs.
Neha: is this the same SKU that had slow NVMe on Friday? might be related to image pull + init ordering.
Tom: metrics: p95 jumped from 180ms -> 1.2s, p99 to 5.6s. streaming stall count +220 across customers over 10min.
Irina (oncall): customer-impact: Support flagged 3 enterprise tenants experiencing dropped streaming frames; feature flagging fallback kicked for one tenant. support-bot raised INC-2026 and added customers CUST-112, CUST-78, CUST-300.
support-bot: Ticket INC-2026 created and linked to account pages: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INC-2026 :white_check_mark:
Tom: trying quick mitigation: ramp down new warmup limit and manually scale pool up by 4 nodes. running command:
```
# manual scale
rctl scale pool d-nj-2 --add 4 --reason "hotburst warmup backlog"
```
Juan: manual scale accepted but new nodes also hit warmup; kernel logs show `OOM while allocating KV cache` for python worker process on two hosts. uploading snippets.
Irina (oncall): okay stop further autoscaler adds; switching to canary fallback policy to smaller model variant. Neha, please flip fallback.
Neha: switching policy now -> `fallback:model=open-6b-quant` for pool d-nj-2. applying: `redwood rollout fallback --pool d-nj-2 --variant open-6b-quant`
Neha: applied. traffic is now being routed to open-6b-quant for ~30% of new sessions. preliminary p99 down to ~2.1s for those sessions.
Tom: reducing prefix caching pressure and evicting stale entries on pool to free KV memory:
```
# evict stale kv
rctl kv evict --pool d-nj-2 --age 30m
```
Juan: mounts recovered on 3 nodes after NFS retry; one node still failing weight load due to corrupted checkpoint. isolating and removing it from rotation.
Irina (oncall): summary for handoff: root cause: dedicated pool d-nj-2 experienced simultaneous warmup failures (NFS + checkpoint corruption) causing autoscaler to attempt large scale-up, but new nodes also faced warmup/OOM leading to queue amplification and p99 SLO breach for streaming. customer impact: 3 enterprise customers had degraded streaming, multiple non-critical developer accounts saw increased retries. Mitigations: manual scale pause, canary fallback to smaller model, KV cache eviction, isolated corrupted host. Current status: p95 ~250ms, p99 ~1.4s (improving), streaming stalls decreasing.
Irina (oncall): handing off to Tom for overnight monitoring and postmortem. please document timeline and add runbook gaps.
Tom: taking over. will keep monitoring for 2h and coordinate hardware team on corrupted checkpoint. action items: (1) add NFS mount health check to warmup (2) add soft cap on autoscaler rapid scale to avoid amplification (3) alert refinement: split warmup timeouts vs steady-state p99.
Neha: i'll open RFC for autoscaler soft-rate limit and fallback test harness.
Juan: i'll replace corrupted checkpoint and run full validation in staging before rejoining pool.
Irina (oncall): thanks team. paging oncall-next at 18:30 UTC for watch. adding notes to incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026/notes
support-bot: Customers notified: CUST-112 (PM), CUST-78 (SRE), CUST-300 (ops). sent templated incident update.
Tom: logs/commands used attached for postmortem. leaving heartbeat here: will check every 15m. :thumbsup:
